content: Goal: Research the main cause of the Bronze Age Collapse.

value: System collapse triggered by Sea Peoples invasions
Ramses III inscription at Medinet Habu

result: Medinet Habu inscriptions detail battles against Peleset and Tjekker, but note massive famine preceding their arrival.

content: Investigate if Sea Peoples were the sole primary cause by looking at Ugarit tablet translations.

result: Letter from king of Ugarit: 'All my troops and chariots are in the Land of Hatti, and all my ships are in the Land of Lukka... The enemy ships have arrived, cities burned.'

content: Ugarit letter suggests sudden military raid, but we need to see if this was isolated. Attempting to match with pottery migration patterns in the Southern Levant.

result: LH IIIC pottery is locally produced imitation of Mycenaean style, suggesting gradual assimilation of refugees rather than a violent invasion force.

content: Refugee pottery style contradicts the sole military invasion theory. The military-only model is a dead-end.
Since famine was noted before the migrations, pivot to climate proxy data showing drought patterns.

result: Pollen and sediment cores from Larnaca Salt Lake show a severe, multi-century drought starting around 1200 BCE.

value: Climate-induced drought caused agricultural failure, driving mass migration and systemic collapse.
Larnaca Lake pollen core data, Kaniewski et al.

content: Conclusion: Severe drought (proven by Larnaca cores) triggered agricultural failure, driving refugee migrations (Sea Peoples) and destroying trade networks, leading to systemic collapse.
